entries.subject: Ortiz et al. (2020) 2018 stellar-occultation ellipse
entries.finding: The README selects the peer-reviewed 2018 occultation ellipse, projected full axes 543.2 ±18 × 459.5 ±11 km, as the displayed shape; the unseen equatorial depth is assumed equal to 543.2 km and the presentation is equator-on, so true three-dimensional flattening stays unresolved.

entries.subject: JPL Horizons elements and independent vectors
entries.finding: The README uses retained Horizons elements, cross-checked against independent vectors, for the heliocentric geometric position at the fixed 2026-09-03 epoch; it states the fixed-epoch two-body orbit does not simulate long-term perturbations.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No surface imagery exists for this body, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid and the README says the normal grid marks unmapped terrain with Shadows off by default.

entries.subject: 2021 occultation preliminary equivalent diameter reported at EPSC 2022
entries.finding: The README records the 2021 event's preliminary equivalent diameter of 500.3 ±2.5 km as supporting the size scale but not replacing the published complete ellipse, so it is not used for the displayed shape.
entries.revisitWhen: The 2021 event is published as a complete peer-reviewed limb solution that can replace the adopted 2018 ellipse.

entries.subject: May 2026 thermal and occultation preprint suggesting a companion
entries.finding: The README states the preprint supports a putative satellite and a larger thermal system size, but infers no confirmed companion shape or primary terrain from it; the displayed model is the primary outline only.
entries.revisitWhen: A companion is confirmed with a published shape or a published primary-body size that supersedes the adopted occultation ellipse.
